explanation: Three-judge 3d DCA panel 'specifically recede[s]' from its own post-1973 Watson, citing only sister-district cases; no en banc, though Rule 9.331 existed from Jan 1980 (own knowledge). Statute change covers Layton, not Watson.

Same three-judge Kentucky panel calls Wilson distinguishable (no judgment/sentence of probation there) and overrules only 'any holding in conflict'; truncated Wilson text cannot show an actual holding was displaced. En banc rule SCR 1.030(7)(d) from own knowledge.

Woods overrules Phillips, but all five judges of the Alabama Court of Criminal Appeals participated (the court sits as a whole; own knowledge), and it relied on the later Alabama Supreme Court decision Ex parte Sorsby.

Three-judge 4th DCA panel in July 1980 recedes from St. John's announced rule on anonymous tips, persuaded only by 2d DCA's Hetland; no higher or en banc authority, though en banc Rule 9.331 was available (own knowledge).

Three-judge 2d DCA panel in 1982 'necessarily recede[s]' from Olcott's remand proviso applying Pearce to resentencing; authorities cited predate Olcott, no en banc or dicta claim; en banc rule existed (own knowledge).
Zimbrick recedes from Urbanek and Tri-State, but eight 4th DCA judges participated (six concurring, two concurring in result), so the court sat en banc, not as a panel.

Three-judge 2d DCA panel recedes from Miles in 1973 on intervening Fifth Circuit constitutional rulings, but Florida DCAs had no en banc procedure until Rule 9.331 in 1980 (own knowledge), so limb 4 fails.
